name: Kelita
overview: Kelita was a male Levite who played a significant role in the religious life of Israel by explaining the law to the people. His service is noted in the book of Nehemiah, specifically in chapter 8 verse 7. Additionally, Kelita's name appears on the sealed covenant document recorded in Nehemiah 10:10, indicating his commitment to the community's covenant obligations.
namesAndTitles: The only recorded name for this individual is Kelita, which appears as a proper name in Nehemiah 8:7. No specific meaning or divine origin of the name is provided in the biblical text.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Kelita as a descendant of the tribe of Levi, emphasizing his priestly lineage. Beyond this tribal affiliation, no further family relationships are recorded in the biblical account.
scriptureSignificance: Kelita's importance lies in his role as a Levite who helped instruct the people in God's law during a critical period of restoration and renewal in Israel. By explaining the law, he contributed to the spiritual education and reformation of the community. His inclusion among those who sealed the covenant in Nehemiah 10 demonstrates his dedication to God's covenant and the communal commitment to follow His statutes.
